$comment: The routing table, as data. route_channel.py, qa_comms.py and render_markdown.py all read this file, so adding a channel is a registry edit plus a producer — not a change in three scripts. 'status' is first-class: a lane with no reachable producer is declared, not commented out, and blocked_by names exactly what is missing. 'coverage_mode' distinguishes a full comm, which must carry every must-land message in scope for its audiences, from a signpost — a banner or a 30-second clip whose job is to carry one message and point at where the detail lives. Holding a signpost to full-comm coverage would force content onto it that the channel library says must not be there. 'requires_signature' says whether the messenger must be named in the copy. A written comm is unattributed without one; a banner carries no signature by nature, and a video's messenger is the on-screen presenter, so demanding the name in the script would force an unnatural line into the read. A channel's 'status' means an automated build chain EXISTS for it — it is not a live check of whether an external account (npm, an MCP connector) is reachable right now. That is what 'preconditions' checks at run time in route_channel.py, which downgrades a 'live' channel to a handoff outcome when a connector precondition (canva_connected, etc.) isn't confirmed available, exactly as it already does for a missing npm package.

skill:docx.name: docx
skill:docx.note: Emits a Node script against the docx (docx-js) package. The package is NOT reliably preinstalled despite the skill's SKILL.md — build_docx.py checks and reports the `npm install -g docx` remedy. Run with NODE_PATH=$(npm root -g).

skill:pptx.name: pptx
skill:pptx.note: Template route is unzip -> edit ppt/slides/slideN.xml -> rezip. Never pptxgenjs when building on a client .potx.

mcp:Canva.note: v0.2 routes through generate-design per the practitioner's decision. create-design-from-brand-template is listed so switching to approved-template autofill is a one-line change once the client has a Brand Template.

local:render_comms_html.name: render_comms_html.py
local:render_comms_html.note: Renders a self-contained, brand-applied HTML artefact directly from the plan and brand profile — no external connector, no design pending client sign-off before anyone can even open it. Needs no MCP server and no npm package, so it never downgrades to a handoff at run time the way mcp:Canva or skill:docx can. canva_brief.py remains available as an alternative route when the client specifically wants a Canva asset or has an approved Canva Brand Template — see channel notes.

mcp:ElevenLabs.note: Verified 2026-08 via the connector registry: installed on the account but DISABLED IN CHAT, and every tool name the directory lists is voice-AGENT management (create_agent, duplicate_agent, get_agent_link, calculate_agent_llm_usage) with three more not shown. No text-to-speech tool is visible. Scope here is the NARRATION TRACK only - the VO script and captions video_spec.py already emits - never the picture. Unblocking is two steps and the second may fail: enable the connector in the chat's connector settings, then re-check whether the tool surface actually exposes TTS.

briefing_deck.label: Briefing deck
notes: With a client .potx: profile_template.py then build_deck.py validate every layout and placeholder before the pptx skill assembles.
Without a .potx: from-scratch build on deck_theme.json, labelled unapproved at handover.
Speaker notes on every content slide are a hard requirement, not a nicety.

newsletter.label: Newsletter
notes: canva_brief.py remains available as an alternative route — run it directly when the client specifically wants a Canva asset, or has an approved channel_specs.newsletter.canva_brand_template_id. The local route is the default because it needs no connector and produces a file the client can open and edit immediately, which is what a Canva design (even an autofilled one) does not.

banner.label: Intranet banner
banner.format: .html (self-contained; works as an on-screen banner and, printed, an A4/A3 notice)
notes: canva_brief.py remains available as an alternative route for the same reason as newsletter's. It was also the ONLY route until this one existed, and it had a sharper defect specific to posters: Canva's generate-design ignores verbatim/held-copy fidelity for image-shaped designs, so the words a designer sees are never guaranteed to be the words QA checked. The local route ships the QA'd words verbatim, always.

edm.label: EDM (email direct mail)
edm.format: .html (email-safe: table layout, inline styles, no external stylesheet)
notes: subject_max_chars is deliberately different from email's 50 — an EDM is a marketing/comms send with its own subject-line convention and mobile-inbox truncation behaviour, not a 1:1 email, so it gets its own limit rather than inheriting email's.

Rendered as table-based HTML with every style inline (no <style> block, no CSS classes, no var()) because mail clients strip or ignore modern CSS unpredictably. Verified only by static markup inspection in this build (reference/channel-library.md's EDM entry names the check) — not by opening the file in a real mail client.

short_form_video.label: Short-form video
short_form_video.blocked_by: ElevenLabs is installed but disabled in this chat, so its tools are not callable. Enable it in the chat's connector settings, then re-check the tool surface: every tool the directory lists today is voice-agent management rather than TTS, so this lane may still have no producer after enabling.

explainer_video.label: Explainer video
explainer_video.format: scene outline + VO script + screen direction
explainer_video.blocked_by: Same as short_form_video: ElevenLabs is disabled in this chat and may not expose TTS even once enabled. Note this lane is only PARTLY served either way - ElevenLabs can narrate, but scene assembly and any presenter avatar remain a human production step. No avatar-video connector exists in the directory: Synthesia has none at all, and the nearest neighbours (HyperFrames by HeyGen, Tella) are different vendors and not installed.
